# AI Voice Agency — full text

AI Voice Agency builds AI phone agents for local service businesses. AVA answers every call in the company's name, books the job on the calendar, and sends the details to the owner right after the call. Built in Kewaskum, Wisconsin; set up for businesses nationwide. Any voice. Any business.

// 02 ── CAPABILITIES
## Dispatch intake, not generic coverage.
[01]
## Reservation Intake
The caller talks normally. The trip fields fill cleanly — pickup, dropoff, date/time, passenger count, vehicle class, bags, notes, contact, corporate account — all captured without a form.
[02]
## Dispatch-Aware Answering
Knows airport transfer vs hourly charter vs wedding vs executive vs shuttle vs last-minute change. Routes urgent to dispatch, escalates VIP and out-of-policy.
[03]
## Rate-Sheet Quoting
Quotes from your rules, not a guess — service area, vehicle classes, airport rules, hourly minimums, zone or mileage, wait-time, meet-and-greet flags. "Estimate only" language where confirmation is required.
[04]
## Flight-Status Concierge
Airline, flight number, terminal, pickup buffer, baggage, greeting notes. Flight-status logic supports timing and dispatcher review. Airport calls get airport context.
[05]
## Greeter Instructions
The AI captures the details your chauffeur needs to nail the airport greet — name for the sign, terminal, baggage claim, curbside vs inside, VIP notes — then hands it clean to the driver. The AI sets it up; your chauffeur delivers it.
[06]
## CRM + Dispatch Writeback
The call ends with a usable reservation record. Writes trip request into your CRM or dispatch software, shared inbox, or queue. Dispatcher confirms instead of rebuilding from scratch.
[07]
## Outbound Lead Recovery Also Does
Caller asked for a quote and disappeared? AVA follows up. Quote-lead callback, missed-call recovery, corporate follow-up, ride confirmations, post-trip surveys. Useful when fleets run lead-gen.
[08]
## Custom Voices
Any voice. Any tone. Any language. Male or female — premium synthetic, or your own cloned voice (even the owner's). Your brand should sound like your brand.
[09]
## Every call + Multilingual
Answers every call, and switches language mid-call when the caller does. Every language your corporate accounts need.
// 03 ── THE CRUSH
## The crush is where this earns its keep.
Friday airport rush. Prom weekend. Concert let-out. Corporate surge. Three callers at once and the next ride goes to whoever answers first. AVA answers the surge, captures the ride, quotes from your rules, texts the passenger, alerts dispatch, and leaves a clean record.
[01]
## Before Hangup
Trip captured, quote given, passenger texted, dispatcher alerted — all before the call ends.
[02]
## Flight-Aware Intake
Airline, terminal, baggage, pickup buffer — captured cleanly and tied to the reservation record for the dispatcher.
[03]
## Dispatch-Ready Record
Reservation lands in your dispatch stack with summary, source, tags, and greeter notes attached. Dispatcher confirms, not rebuilds.
[04]
## Surge Absorption
Built for burst capacity, scoped to your call volume. When everyone calls at the same moment, none of them get voicemail.

// 06 ── COMMON QUESTIONS
## Questions operators ask.
[01]
## What does AVA actually do on a reservation call?
AVA answers, captures pickup, drop-off, date and time, passenger count, vehicle class, bags, contact, corporate account, and any notes — then quotes from your rate rules, captures greeter instructions for airport runs, writes a clean reservation record into your dispatch stack, and alerts the dispatcher before the caller hangs up.
[02]
## Does AVA work alongside my dispatch software?
Yes. It connects to CRMs too. We check your reservation software and handle the connection. Your dispatcher confirms; AVA doesn't dispatch the driver.
[03]
## Can AVA quote from our rate sheet?
Yes. AVA quotes from your rules — service area, vehicle classes, airport rules, hourly minimums, zone or mileage, wait-time, and meet-and-greet flags — with "estimate only" language where confirmation is required.
[04]
## How does AVA handle airport runs?
AVA captures airline, flight number, terminal, pickup buffer, baggage notes, and greeting preferences. Flight-status logic supports timing and dispatcher review. The AI captures the meet-and-greet detail — your chauffeur delivers it.
[05]
## Will AVA replace my dispatcher?
No. AVA takes the intake load so the dispatcher dispatches. Three calls hit at once — AVA takes all three, captures the trips, and the dispatcher works the manifests instead of fighting the phones.
[06]
## What about a Friday afternoon airport surge?
Built for burst capacity, scoped to your call volume. AVA answers the surge, captures the ride, quotes from your rules, texts the passenger, alerts dispatch, and leaves a clean record. No more voicemail leak when the next ride goes to whoever answers first.
[07]
## Does AVA do outbound for ground transportation?
Yes — inbound is the lead capability, but AVA also handles quote-lead callbacks, missed-call recovery, corporate account follow-up, ride confirmations, and post-trip surveys. Useful for fleets running lead-gen to keep vehicles full.

// 01 ── THE CRUSH
## Why Wisconsin operators lose runs.
[01] Friday 4:47 PM — the corporate-confirm wave hits. Five clients call within twelve minutes to confirm Friday-night pickups. Your dispatcher is on line one. Lines two through five hit voicemail. Three of those clients book your competitor by 5:15.
[02] Packers home Sunday — Ashwaubenon and Lambeau shuttle requests fill every line in your operation for the three-hour pregame window. You either turn down work or hire a part-time dispatcher you only need ten days a year.
[03] Overnight Marriott concierge calls a 2 AM Mitchell airport pickup. Your night line forwards to a cell that hits voicemail. The concierge dials the next operator. You lose the trip and a TMC relationship that took two years to build.
[04] Capacity hits ceiling on a wedding-week Saturday. Three corporate clients call needing same-day SUV pickups. You'd farm them through GNet to your affiliate — except your dispatcher is running three confirms at once and the affiliate-farm window closes.
[05] A new prospect calls asking for a stretch quote. Your dispatcher is on a call. The caller leaves a voicemail. By the time you call back, they've already booked. The lead-acquisition cost of getting them to dial you in the first place — gone.

// MAY 11, 2026 · WISCONSIN LIMO · 4 MIN READ
## How Wisconsin Limo Operators Are Beating The Crush With AI.
Every limo operator in Wisconsin knows the window. Friday afternoon. 4:30 to 5:30 PM. The corporate book confirms. The weekend bookings stack. The first wave of after-work clients books a Saturday-night dinner pickup. The phone lines flood for sixty minutes and then the volume drops off a cliff.
The dispatch industry calls it The Crush. If you've run a phone-heavy operation in this state, you don't need anyone to tell you what The Crush is — you've lived it. The question is how much of it you're catching, and how much you're losing.
## The math nobody runs
Take a five-vehicle Wisconsin operator. Friday afternoon, 4:30 to 5:30 PM. Average inbound call volume for that window: eighteen calls. Average operator with a single dispatcher catches maybe twelve of them — the rest hit voicemail.
Six calls a week. Average call value across confirms, new bookings, and quote requests: $220. That's $1,320 a week, $5,280 a month, $68,640 a year. From a single hour on a single day.
Now add the second-order effect. The corporate concierge at the Marriott calls your line at 2 AM for an airport pickup. Hits voicemail. Calls your competitor. Books your competitor. Next time the concierge has an airport pickup, they default to your competitor — not because they prefer them, but because they remember which line picked up. Six months later you're not in the rotation. That's not $220 in lost revenue. That's a relationship.
## Why dispatchers can't fix it
The instinct is to hire another dispatcher. The numbers don't work. A Wisconsin dispatcher costs you roughly $42,000 a year fully loaded. They cover one or maybe two phone lines at once. They don't work overnight. They take lunch. They get sick.
The actual phone problem is variance. Most hours of most days, one dispatcher is overstaffed. The Crush hour, Lambeau game Sunday, the New Year's surge — those are the hours where you need eight dispatchers, not one. No staffing model handles that variance profitably.
This is why operators stay with the loss. The math on hiring doesn't pencil. The math on losing the calls doesn't either — but the lost calls don't sit on a P&L the way a salary does. You feel the loss; you don't see it.
## What an AI phone agent actually does at 4:47 PM
AVA answers every call. Eighteen calls in an hour or a surge all at once — same intake every time, no voicemail leakage.
For a corporate confirm: AVA recognizes the account, pulls the standing instructions, confirms the pickup time and vehicle, and sends dispatch the trip sheet. It works beside Limo Anywhere, FASTTRAK, Livery Coach or whatever you run. Your dispatcher sees a confirmed trip in their queue, not a missed call.
For a new lead: AVA captures the pickup location, drop-off, vehicle preference, passenger count, and contact details. Pushes a lead file to your CRM with the full intake. Your dispatcher follows up with pricing instead of starting from a voicemail.
AVA's limo product is AI Chauffeur.
For an overflow scenario where your fleet is at capacity: AVA can farm the trip via GNet to your affiliate network, keeping the commission and the relationship instead of losing the work entirely.
None of this replaces your dispatcher. AVA replaces the intake. Your dispatcher still confirms drivers, runs manifests, and works the operation. They just stop drowning in the first wave of phone calls so they can do the work that actually moves the manifest.
## What it costs vs what it saves
AVA Starter is $497 a month plus $497 setup. For a five-vehicle operator losing $5,280 a month to missed Crush calls, that's a ten-week payback on the math you can see — and the relationships you can't immediately measure stack on top.
For a 4-15 vehicle operation that needs scheduling, CRM handoffs, and peak-hour coverage, Growth at $997 a month plus $1,500 setup runs the math even harder.
The point is not to sell you a plan. The point is that the calls you're losing are paying for the system several times over — and you're already paying for them, just on the lost-revenue side of the ledger.
## The fix, without the hiring
The move is simple: stop trying to staff The Crush. Let AVA handle the surge, write the trips, and route the affiliate overflow — so your dispatchers get their Friday afternoons back instead of drowning in the first wave, and your corporate book stops leaking to whoever picks up faster.
You don't have to take my word for it. The demo line is (414) 240-8930. Call it. Hear AVA answer the call. Talk through a sample limo intake. Thirty seconds and you'll hear what your callers will hear.
If it sounds right, the scoping call is twenty minutes. Operator to operator. We figure out if it fits your operation. Pricing on the transportation page. The full Wisconsin-limo wedge with operator pain detail is over here.

## Can it book appointments on my calendar?
Yes. AVA offers open times from your calendar and books the job while the customer is on the phone. The customer gets a confirmation text.
Yes. When AVA is set up for a business, it books the job on the business's calendar during the call. Customers call, explain what they need and book the appointment in the same conversation.
AVA answers calls and books jobs. Answers every call. Knows your business. Quotes your rates. Books the job.
Here is how a booking call goes.
- The phone rings on the number customers already call. AVA answers every call, day or night, in the business's name.
- AVA takes the details: the caller's name, phone number, address and what they need. A water heater that quit. A roof leak after a storm. A first visit for a new patient. A cut and color.
- It knows the services, the hours and the service area, so it books only what the business does, where the business works.
- If the caller asks about cost, AVA quotes the rates the business gave it.
- AVA offers open times from the calendar. The caller picks one, and AVA books it.
- The customer gets a confirmation text with the time.
The booking word fits the trade. A plumber gets a service visit on the calendar. A roofer gets an estimate visit. A salon gets the appointment. A dental office gets the new-patient visit.
Every job lands on your calendar, in your CRM, your texts and your inbox, with the recording and the transcript. If a detail looks off, you can play the call or read what was said.
What if a call should not wait for an open time? The owner decides what counts as urgent, like a burst pipe or no heat in winter. AVA sends those calls to the owner's cell.
What if AVA can't handle a call? It follows the owner's choice: send the call to the owner's cell, take a message, or set up a callback.
Booking works the same on a weeknight, on a Sunday, or when the team is already on another call.
What stays with you: the calendar is yours. The times you leave open are the times callers are offered. You set the rates and the hours, you decide which calls go to your cell, and you can change any of it.
## Questions
## Does the caller pick the time?
Yes. AVA offers open times from the calendar and books the one the caller picks.
## How does the caller know the job is booked?
The customer gets a confirmation text with the appointment time.
## Where does the booking show up for the owner?
Every job lands on your calendar, in your CRM, your texts and your inbox.

## Does it answer the phone at 3 AM?
Yes. AVA answers every call at any hour, quotes your rates and books the job. Every job lands in your CRM, your texts and your inbox.
Yes. When AVA is set up for a business, it answers every call, and a call at 3 AM gets the same booking conversation as a call at 3 PM.
AVA answers calls and books jobs. Answers every call. Knows your business. Quotes your rates. Books the job. The hour does not change any of that.
Here is how a 3 AM call goes.
- The phone rings on the number customers already call. AVA answers in the business's name.
- The caller says what is wrong. The furnace quit. A pipe burst under the sink. A tooth cracked at dinner.
- AVA takes the details that matter: name, phone number, address and what the caller needs.
- If the caller asks what it costs, AVA quotes the rates the business gave it at setup.
- AVA offers open times from the calendar and books the job while the customer is still on the phone. For a plumber that is a service visit. For a dental office it is an appointment.
- The customer gets a confirmation text with the time.
Every job lands on your calendar, in your CRM, your texts and your inbox. The recording and the transcript come with it. In the morning the job is already there, and the call shows on the dashboard with every other call.
What about a call that should not wait for morning? The owner decides which calls are urgent, like no heat in winter or water coming through a ceiling. AVA hands those calls to someone on the team, or sends them to the owner's cell.
What if AVA can't handle a call? It follows the choice the owner made at setup: send the call to the owner's cell, take a message, or set up a callback.
The same thing happens on a Sunday, on a holiday, or when the team is already on another call. The owner picks the coverage: every call, only after hours, or only the calls the team can't get to.
What stays with you: you set the rates, the hours and the calendar. You decide which calls go to your cell and what happens when AVA can't handle one. You can change any of it. Your team still does the work.

## What does the owner get after a call?

## Can it take more than one call at a time?

Yes. When AVA is set up for a business, every call is answered, even when several customers call at the same time. No caller waits for a line to open, and no caller hears a busy signal.

With one person on the phone, the second caller hears ringing or voicemail, and may call the next company on the list. With AVA, each caller gets a real conversation right away.

- A customer calls the business number. AVA picks up.

- While that call is going, a second customer calls. AVA answers that call too, and runs the same steps.
- Every call is recorded and written out, so each conversation is saved on its own, even when two happened at once.
- Right after each call, the job is on the record. Every job lands on your calendar, in your CRM, your texts and your inbox.
That is the whole idea in four short lines. Answers every call. Knows your business. Quotes your rates. Books the job.

What stays with you: your team, your customers and your schedule. When a busy morning brings a stack of calls at once, your people can stay with the customer in front of them. Each caller still talks to AVA right away, and each booked job waits for you with the recording and the written-out call on your own dashboard.
